intended_object: For a continuous map g : X → Y and an abelian sheaf A on Y, the canonical base-change comparison morphism g⁻¹(forget A) → forget(g⁻¹A). It goes from the inverse image of the underlying sheaf of sets to the underlying sheaf of sets of the inverse-image abelian sheaf, and is obtained as the mate of the forgetful functor applied to the unit of pullback ⊣ pushforward. Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and the later results in the file (naturality, isomorphism, compatibility with identity and composition).
explanation: The body applies `underlyingSheaf Y` (sheafCompose with the forgetful functor from AddCommGrpCat) to the unit η_A : A → g₊g⁻¹A of the abelian-group pullback ⊣ pushforward adjunction. This gives forget A → forget(g₊g⁻¹A). Since forget ∘ g₊ is definitionally g₊ ∘ forget (the file uses this as `rfl` in `commMap`), the map has type forget A → g₊(forget g⁻¹A). The body then transposes it through the inverse of the Type-valued adjunction's hom-equivalence, giving g⁻¹(forget A) → forget(g⁻¹A). This is exactly the standard definition of the comparison map as the mate of the forgotten unit. The file goes on to prove it natural, compatible with identity and composition of pullbacks, and an isomorphism for every continuous map. That is the expected property, since the forgetful functor commutes with sheaf pullback. This is one specific canonical morphism, and abelian groups to sets is the case the sheaf-cohomology library needs. Mathlib only provides the general mate machinery (`mateEquiv`), not a named version of this comparison, so the definition is neither wrong nor too narrow.
